text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorkInLibrary(x) ::: x currently works in the library.
FromCSDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakingCourse(x, y) ::: x is taking course y.
Course(y) ::: y is a course.
Professor(y) ::: y is a professor.
WorksWithProfessor(x, y) ::: x is taking a class with professor y.
Lab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
James ::: James (constant).
Premises:
¬∃x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLibrary(x) ∧ ¬FromCSDept(x)) ::: None of the students who currently work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (PartTimeJob(x) ∧ OfferedByUniversity(x) → WorkInLibrary(x)) ::: All students with part-time jobs offered by the university currently work in the library.
∀x (TakingCourse(x, databaseCourse) → FromCSDept(x)) ::: All students taking the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (TakingCourse(x, databaseCourse) → TakingClassWith(x, ProfessorDavid)) ::: All students taking a class with Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorkInLab(x) → TakingClassWith(x, ProfessorDavid)) ::: All students working in the lab are taking a class with Professor David.
WorkInLab(James) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(WorkInLab(James) ∨ HasPartTimeJob(James)) ::: James doesn't work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.
Conclusion:
TakingCourse(James, databaseCourse) ::: James takes the database course.
